callaway-elyte: Long and forgiving with a clean look, often winning fittings; a few cracked crowns or failed heads.
callaway-elyte-mini: Straight and forgiving, with more fairways for about 10 yards less; a few report crown cracks.
callaway-elyte-triple-diamond: Lower spin, more distance and tighter dispersion, but a few find it fade biased and hard to launch.
callaway-quantum-mini: Straighter off the tee with little or no distance lost, though one misses a big driver on par 5s.
callaway-quantum-triple-diamond: Lower spin and more distance once fitted; a couple found it not enough of a step up for the money.
callaway-quantum-triple-diamond-max: Longer and lower spinning while keeping forgiveness, though a few found it hard feeling or loud.
cobra-ds-adapt-max-k: Mishits and slices stay in play, and it often costs less than rivals; some note a draw bias.
cobra-ds-adapt-x: Adjustable weight helps and forgiveness beats expectations; one sim test had it missing both ways.
ping-g430-max: Draw weight helps slicers and it is easy to hit straight; some see too much spin or high launch.
ping-g430-max-10k: Keeps big slices in play and finds far more fairways; a fair number report cracked crowns.
ping-g440-k: Mishits stay in play and slices are tamed, but good hits can be a bit shorter than other drivers.
ping-g440-max: Very forgiving and straight, for dispersion over distance; not always longest on centre hits.
taylormade-qi35-ls: Distance and low spin with tight dispersion for better strikers; several faces popped within weeks.
taylormade-qi35-max: Long and forgiving, with fitting results beating other drivers; the main complaint is early cracks.
taylormade-qi4d: Long, straight and forgiving, often beating other brands at fittings; a minority could not hit it.
taylormade-qi4d-ls: Low spin and faster ball speed than an old driver; a couple find it harder to hit than the Max.
taylormade-r7-quad-mini: Much straighter as a driver replacement, giving up 10 to 15 yards; a few could not launch it.
titleist-gt2: More distance and straighter shots with praised feel; cracked crowns are the common complaint.
titleist-gt280-mini: Much straighter in place of a driver or 3-wood and easy off the deck, though it costs some distance.
titleist-gt3: Long, low spinning and great feeling, but less forgiving than the GT2, with some snap hooks.
titleist-gts2: Very forgiving, with off-centre strikes losing little; one questions the gain over a GT2.
callaway-quantum-max: Draw-bias weighting and loft adjustment help slicers find fairways, though some still slice it.
ping-g430-lst: Long with tight dispersion for those fitted well, but several report cracked heads or crowns.
callaway-elyte-x: Straighter than an old driver with lower spin, though a couple still slice it.
titleist-gt4: Low spin for those who need it; a few report cracks in the head.
ping-g430-sft: Straight and forgiving, with mishits that still go; a few say it is loud.
cobra-ds-adapt-ls: Low spin and fast ball speed with adjustable options; a few report a buckled or shattered head.
